label: copy-phase input g (fed-back g from original position >= 2)
explanation: Token-specific copy-phase feature: fires only when the fed-back input token is the letter g during the copy phase (after <DEL>). It never fires in the original phase, on the delimiter, or on any other input token. It is essentially silent when the copied g came from original position 0 or 1 (recall_idx <= 2): those few activations are tiny and hold 0.1% of mass. Magnitude grows with how late g sat in the original sequence; the strongest activations come from g at original positions 4-7. When gg repeats, the second g is usually somewhat weaker. Most false positives are early-position g (original position 2) in longer sequences.

issues: Factual claims hold up. The feature never fires in the original or delimiter phase (0 active steps in each). On the dev split, 56813 of 56814 active steps have in_tok g (1 stray j). Copy-phase g at recall_idx 0-1 never fires, and recall_idx 2 (g from original position 1) has precision 0.018 and 0.06% of the mass. The test numbers reproduce: P 0.976, R 0.995, F1 0.985, mass recall 0.999.

False positives are a boundary effect, not a separate class of input. At recall_idx==3 (g from original position 2) precision is 0.916, versus 0.9999 for recall_idx>=4. Splitting by length gives 0.960 for L<=5 and 0.888 for L>=7, so the claim that longer sequences produce more of the FPs is right. Dropping recall_idx==3 would lose about 10% of the mass, so the threshold of >=3 is the right call.

The magnitude claim checks out. Mass per active step is about 7e-6 at recall_idx 3, 1.8e-5 at 4, and a plateau of about 2.3e-5 at 5-8. That puts the top activations at original positions 4-7, as stated.

The gg claim is weakly supported at best. Among predicted steps, prev_tok==g has the same precision (0.978) as the rest, and its average mass per step (~1.7e-5) is close to the overall average. Saying the second g is 'usually weaker' may overstate it, but this is minor and does not change the predicate.
The 'correct' flag doesn't matter: only 3 predicted steps have correct==0. The label's 'original position >= 2' matches recall_idx>=3, because the input at copy step t is the original token at t-L-1.
